title: Sensation and perception
note: Sensation is detection: receptors turn physical energy into neural signals (transduction). Perception is interpretation: the brain organizes those signals using both the incoming data (bottom-up) and what it already knows and expects (top-down).

read.title: Seeing is partly believing
text: Your eyes do not send the brain a finished picture. Light passes through the cornea and lens and lands on the retina, where rods and cones transduce it into neural signals. Cones, packed into the fovea, give color and sharp detail in good light. Rods, spread across the rest of the retina, work in dim light and catch motion at the edges of vision.

Those signals are only raw material. Perception builds a world from them using two streams at once. Bottom-up processing works from the data: a sudden flash pulls your eyes toward it. Top-down processing works from knowledge and expectation: you find your keys faster by looking where you usually leave them.

Because attention is limited, people can miss what is right in front of them. In studies of inattentional blindness, viewers busy counting basketball passes often fail to notice a person in a gorilla suit walking through the scene.

The brain also groups what it sees in predictable ways, as the Gestalt psychologists described. Items close together seem to belong together, similar items form groups, and gaps get filled to make complete shapes.
